summary: Daniel Veidlinger is a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies. He earned his PhD at the University of Chicago under Steven Collins, and also studied under Nalini Devdas and Samli Mulkæo. He has been a professor at California State University, Chico since 2003.

Daniel W. Kent is a scholar of religious and Buddhist studies. He earned his Ph.D. at the University of Virginia, where he was attested as an instructor in 2010 alongside an instructor post at Mary Baldwin University.

Daniel Wojahn specializes in Tibetology and history/archaeology. He completed an MA at the University of Leipzig and a DPhil at the University of Oxford (2019–2024). His academic posts include roles at Oxford, Bonn, and an associate researcher position at the University of Vienna (2025).

Daniel Wright (1833–1902) was a scholar in the fields of indology and history/archaeology. He studied at the University of St Andrews around 1849–1853 and served as a physician at the British Residency in Nepal from 1866 to 1876.

Daniela Berti works in indology and religious studies. She studied at Sapienza University of Rome, the University of Siena (PhD), and Paris Nanterre University (HDR). She has served as a senior researcher at the CNRS and taught as an ATER at INALCO (2001–2003).

Daniela Bevilacqua specializes in indology and religious studies. She earned degrees from Sapienza University of Rome and Paris Nanterre University (PhD). She held research posts at SOAS (2015–2020) and Iscte – University Institute of Lisbon (2023), and lectured at the University of Turin (2021).

Daniela De Simone works in history, archaeology, Buddhist studies, and indology. She completed an MSc at LSE and a PhD at the University of Naples "L'Orientale". Her positions include research curator at the British Museum (2016–2020) and permanent member at Ghent University (2021).

Daniele Cuneo is an academic whose posts include affiliations with the University of Paris and the Sorbonne (attested 2018), as well as a faculty position at the University of Texas at Austin (attested 2026).
Danielle Feller is an indologist who earned her PhD from the University of Lausanne in 2001. She completed her doctoral studies under Johannes Bronkhorst and also studied under Ganesh U. Thite.
Danny M.C. Ching is a scholar in Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and Sinology. He is a PhD student at Columbia University, attested in 2023 and 2026.

Danping Long is a scholar in indology and Buddhist studies. As of 2026, she is attested as a doctoral student at the University of Munich and a Doktorandin at the Göttingen Academy of Sciences and Humanities.

Danuta Stasik is an indologist who studied at the University of Warsaw under Maria Byrski from around 1975 to 1980. Beginning in 1986, she held the Chair of South Asian Studies in the Faculty of Oriental Studies at the University of Warsaw.

Daoquan Yu (1901–1992) was a Tibetologist and linguist. He studied at Cheeloo University and under Jacques Bacot in Paris, later serving as a professor at Minzu University of China from circa 1953 to 1992.

Dasharatha Sharma (1903–1976) was an Indian historian and indologist educated at the University of Delhi. He served as a reader at the University of Delhi, professor and dean at Jai Narain Vyas University, and director of the Rajasthan Oriental Research Institute.

Daud Ali is a historian and indologist. He studied at the College of William & Mary and the University of Chicago under Ronald Inden. He taught history at SOAS (circa 1995–2009) before becoming an associate professor at the University of Pennsylvania in 2009.
David A. Dilworth is a scholar in philosophy and Japanology. He studied under Masao Abe and Valdo H. Viglielmo, and he taught Steve Odin.

David A. Hall is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Japanology who earned his doctorate from UC Berkeley in 1990 and studied under Shoshin Ichishima. He was a visiting scholar at Taisho University (1977) and department chair at Montgomery College (attested 2019).
David Aberle (1918–2004) studied at Harvard University, the University of New Mexico, and Columbia University. He held an academic post at the University of British Columbia from circa 1967 to 1983.
David Azzopardi specializes in Buddhist and religious studies. He completed his PhD at SOAS University of London under the supervision of Kate Crosby (attested 2010).

David B. Gray is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and religious studies. He completed his Ph.D. at Columbia University under Robert A. F. Thurman and Ryuichi Abe. He was a postdoctoral fellow at Rice University and an assistant professor at Santa Clara University.
